```{r}
#| label: set-up-environment
#| include: false

# set wd
setwd("/mnt/Genomics/Working/libby.natola/home/libby.natola/projects/BioMarathon/barcoding_data/")

# packages
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(vegan)
library(hydroTSM)
library(scales)
library(plotly)
library(lme4)
library(glmmTMB)
library(patchwork)
library(ggrepel)

# load data
sd <- read_excel("QHAK2_Dec2025.xlsx", sheet = "Samples") 

# update the sd so that if the species is NA, the identifier gets the column name (the rank) of whatever was the lowest identifiable rank tacked onto the identifier (eg something identified to Nereis would be called Nereis genus)
sd <- sd %>% 
    rename(Phylum = `Phylum...6`,
         bin_type = `BIN TYPE`,
         CollectionDate = `Collection Date...29`,
         Depth = `Depth...11`) %>%
  mutate(Identification_and_rank = case_when(
      !is.na(Species) ~ Identification,
      !is.na(Genus) ~ paste(Identification, "genus"),
      !is.na(Tribe) ~ paste(Identification, "tribe"),
      !is.na(Subfamily) ~ paste(Identification, "subfamily"),
      !is.na(Family) ~ paste(Identification, "family"),
      !is.na(Order) ~ paste(Identification, "order"),
      !is.na(Class) ~ paste(Identification, "class"),
      TRUE ~ Identification),
      bin_type = case_when(bin_type == "Unique" ~ "Novel BINs",
                           bin_type == "Non-unique" ~ "Previously in BOLD",
                           TRUE ~ bin_type),
    bin_type = factor(bin_type, levels = c("Previously in BOLD", "Novel BINs")),
    CollectionDate = as.Date(CollectionDate, format = "%d-%b-%Y"),
         month = as.numeric(format(CollectionDate, "%m")),
         month_text = month(month, label = TRUE, abbr = TRUE),
         year = as.numeric(format(CollectionDate, "%Y")),
    season = time2season(CollectionDate, out.fmt = "seasons"),
    Depth = as.numeric(Depth),
    Depth_bin = cut(Depth, 
                    breaks = seq(0, ceiling(max(Depth, na.rm = TRUE) / 50) * 50, by = 50),
                          include.lowest = TRUE),
    Depth_bin_display = str_remove_all(Depth_bin, "[\\(\\)\\[\\]]"),
    Depth_bin_display = str_replace(Depth_bin_display, "," , "-"),
    Depth_bin_display = factor(Depth_bin_display,
                               levels = c("0-50", "50-100", "100-150", "150-200", "200-250", "250-300"),
                               labels = c("0-50", "51-100", "101-150", "151-200", "201-250", "251-300")))


# set theme
theme_set(
  theme_bw() +
    theme(
      panel.spacing.y = unit(3, "lines"),
      axis.text.x = element_text(
        angle = 45,
        hjust = 1,
        margin = margin(t = 10)
      )
    )
)

novel_pal <- c("#4472c4", "#bdd7ee")
```

### Samples per phylum

The first was the number of samples assigned to each phylum:

```{r}
#| label: phylum-histogram

phylum_hist <- sd %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = fct_infreq(Phylum))) + 
  geom_histogram(stat = "count", fill = "#4472c4") + 
  labs(x = "Phylum", y = "Total Samples") 

# get that order
phylum_order <- sd$Phylum %>% fct_infreq() %>% levels()
sd <- sd %>% 
  mutate(Phylum = factor(Phylum, levels = phylum_order))

ggsave("plots/biomarathon_barcoding_samples_per_phylum.png", plot = phylum_hist, 
       height = 5, width = 8, units = "in", dpi = 400)

ggplotly(phylum_hist)
```

### Novel bins

The second was the percent of BINs that were unique per phylum:

```{r}
#| label: phylum-pct-unique

phylum_pct_bar <- sd %>% 
  group_by(Phylum, bin_type) %>% 
  summarise(n = n_distinct(BIN), .groups = "drop") %>% 
  filter(!is.na(bin_type)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = Phylum, y = n, fill = bin_type)) + 
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent, breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Previously in BOLD" = novel_pal[2],
    "Novel BINs" = novel_pal[1])) +
  labs(x = "Phylum", y = "Percent of BINs", fill = NULL) 

ggsave("plots/biomarathon_barcoding_pct_unique_per_phylum.png", plot = phylum_pct_bar, 
       height = 5, width = 8, units = "in", dpi = 400)

ggplotly(phylum_pct_bar)

```

```{r}
#| label: samples_and_pctunique_phylum
samples_pct_unique_phylum <- phylum_hist / phylum_pct_bar + plot_annotation(tag_levels = 'A')

ggsave("plots/biomarathon_barcoding_samples_and_pct_unique_per_phylum.png", plot = samples_pct_unique_phylum, 
       height = 10, width = 7, units = "in", dpi = 400)
```

### Samples x novel BINS

Then I recreated the scatter plot where each point represents a phylum and the x-axis shows the number of samples assigned to that phylum and the y-axis shows the percent of BINs in that phylum that are novel.

```{r}
#| label: samples-x-novel-bins

# get a row for each phylum, get number of samples in phylum, get number of novel bins in each phylum
sample_sums <- sd %>% 
  group_by(Phylum) %>% 
  summarise(num_samples = n())
  
samples_novel_bins_bar <- sd %>% 
  group_by(Phylum, bin_type) %>% 
  summarise(novel_bins = n_distinct(BIN), groups = "drop") %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = bin_type, values_from = novel_bins, values_fill = 0) %>% 
  select(-`NA`) %>% 
  mutate(pct_uq = `Novel BINs`/(`Previously in BOLD`+`Novel BINs`)) %>% 
  select(-`Previously in BOLD`, -`Novel BINs`) %>% 
  left_join(sample_sums, by = "Phylum") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = num_samples, y = pct_uq)) +
  geom_point(color = "#4472c4") + 
  labs(x = "Number of samples", y = "Novel BINs") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent, breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1))

ggsave("plots/biomarathon_barcoding_novel_bins_per_sample.png", plot = samples_novel_bins_bar, 
       height = 5, width = 8, units = "in", dpi = 400)

ggplotly(samples_novel_bins_bar)

samples_novel_bins_bar_phylumlabs <- samples_novel_bins_bar + 
  geom_text_repel(
    aes(label = Phylum),
    size = 3,
    max.overlaps = Inf,
    box.padding = 0.6,
    point.padding = 0.3,
    segment.color = "grey60") 

samples_novel_bins_bar_phylumlabs

ggsave("plots/biomarathon_barcoding_novel_bins_per_sample_phylumlabs.png", 
       plot = samples_novel_bins_bar_phylumlabs, 
       height = 5, width = 8, units = "in", dpi = 400)

```

### BIN accumulation curve

Finally, I recreated the BIN accumulation curve. I'm not sure exactly how Matt made this so I used the specaccum function on a sample x BIN matrix from vegan and came up with something similar to Matt's.

```{r}
#| label: bin-accumulation-curve
#| cache: true

# build a sample x BIN incidence matrix
bin_matrix <- sd %>%
  filter(!is.na(BIN)) %>% 
  distinct(`Sample ID...1`, BIN) %>%
  mutate(present = 1) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = BIN, values_from = present, values_fill = 0) %>% 
  column_to_rownames("Sample ID...1")

set.seed(123)
bin_accum <- specaccum(bin_matrix, method = "random", permutations = 999)

accum_df <- data.frame(
  samples = bin_accum$sites,
  bins = bin_accum$richness
)

bin_accumulation_curve <- ggplot(accum_df, aes(x = samples, y = bins)) +
  geom_line(color = "#4472c4", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = "Number of samples", y = "Cumulative count of BINs") +
  theme_classic()

ggsave("plots/biomarathon_barcoding_bin_accumulation_curve.png", plot = bin_accumulation_curve, 
       height = 5, width = 8, units = "in", dpi = 400)

ggplotly(bin_accumulation_curve)
```

```{r}
#| label: samples_and_accumulation
novel_bins_and_accumulation <- samples_novel_bins_bar / bin_accumulation_curve + plot_annotation(tag_levels = 'A', )

ggsave("plots/biomarathon_barcoding_novel_per_sample+accumulation_curve.png", plot = novel_bins_and_accumulation, 
       height = 10, width = 7, units = "in", dpi = 400)

novel_bins_and_accumulation_phylumlabs <- samples_novel_bins_bar_phylumlabs / bin_accumulation_curve + plot_annotation(tag_levels = 'A', )

ggsave("plots/biomarathon_barcoding_novel_per_sample_phylumlabs+accumulation_curve.png", plot = novel_bins_and_accumulation_phylumlabs, 
       height = 10, width = 7, units = "in", dpi = 400)

```

### Time

First we wanted to compare novel vs non-novel bins by month to see if there are times of year when we get more novel taxa than others.

```{r}
#| label: novel-x-month
#| fig-height: 12

num_novel_month <- sd %>% 
  group_by(bin_type, month, month_text, year) %>% 
  summarise(n = n_distinct(BIN), .groups = "drop") %>% 
  filter(!is.na(bin_type) & !is.na(month) & !is.na(year)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = month_text, y = n, fill = bin_type)) + 
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  facet_wrap(~ year, ncol = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = novel_pal) + 
  labs(x = "Month", y = "Number of BINs", fill = NULL)+
  theme(panel.spacing.y = unit(0.2, "lines"))

ggsave("plots/biomarathon_barcoding_novel_per_month.png", plot = num_novel_month, 
       height = 10, width = 8, units = "in", dpi = 400)

ggplotly(num_novel_month)

pct_novel_month_years <- sd %>% 
  filter(!is.na(bin_type) & !is.na(month) & !is.na(year)) %>% 
  group_by(bin_type, month, month_text, year) %>% 
  summarise(n = n_distinct(BIN), .groups = "drop") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = month_text, y = n, fill = bin_type)) + 
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  facet_wrap(~ year, ncol = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Previously in BOLD" = novel_pal[2],
    "Novel BINs" = novel_pal[1])) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "Month", y = "Percent of BINs", fill = NULL)+
  theme(panel.spacing.y = unit(0.2, "lines"))

ggsave("plots/biomarathon_barcoding_pct_novel_per_month_years_sep.png", plot = pct_novel_month_years, 
       height = 10, width = 8, units = "in", dpi = 400)

ggplotly(pct_novel_month_years)

```

```{r}
#| label: novel-x-month-glmm

# convert to wide format 
sd_wide <- sd %>% 
    group_by(bin_type, month, year) %>% 
    summarise(n = n_distinct(BIN), .groups = "drop") %>% 
    filter(!is.na(bin_type) & !is.na(month) & !is.na(year)) %>% 
    pivot_wider(names_from = bin_type, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>% 
    mutate(total = `Novel BINs` + `Previously in BOLD`) 

m1 <- glmer(cbind(`Novel BINs`, total - `Novel BINs`) ~ factor(month) + (1 | year),
            data = sd_wide, family = binomial)
m1

m2 <- glmmTMB(cbind(`Novel BINs`, total - `Novel BINs`) ~ factor(month) + (1 | year),
              data = sd_wide, family = betabinomial)
m2

m0 <- glm(cbind(`Novel BINs`, total - `Novel BINs`) ~ factor(month), data = sd_wide, family = binomial)
m0
anova(m0)   # or AIC(m0, m1, m2) — expect m0 to fit essentially as well, with fewer params

m_null <- glm(cbind(`Novel BINs`, total - `Novel BINs`) ~ 1, data = sd_wide, family = binomial)
m_null
anova(m_null, m0, test = "Chisq")
```

I tested the relationship between month and BIN novelty with a few statistical tests. I started with GLMM because there was a lot of variation in number of samples sequenced across months and years, because we are really interested in the proportions of novel BINs per month rather than the counts, and because the same months were sampled repeatedly across multiple years, I wanted to try a year-level random effect. I ran it both with and without the beta binomial family and checked these for overdispersion. They both showed the random effect was 0 so year doesn't affect these models and we don't need to include it. The beta binomial GLMM had a very high dispersion parameter, indicating negligible extra-binomial variance (it effectively converges to a standard binomial) so the beta-binomial fit wasn't needed either. Therefore, I decided to just run a regular GLM, which had a lower AIC (124.8) than the binomial GLMM (126.8) (beta-binomial GLMM was unable to converge and has AIC of NA). I ran an ANOVA of the GLM comparing this model to an intercept-only null model which was non-significant (χ² = 11.52, df = 10, p = 0.32), giving no evidence of a monthly effect on BIN novelty p-value was 0.32 so no pattern by month. I also ran a null model to compare against the GLM and found the null model had a lower AIC (116.4), confirming there's no pattern associated with month.

```{r}

It looks like maybe there are more BINs detected in April overall, we have highest non-unique and unique BINs in April 2021-2023. Percentage-wise I'm not seeing much of a pattern.

  summarise(season_sum = n_distinct(BIN)) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(bin_type)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = season, y = season_sum, fill = bin_type)) + 
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  facet_wrap(~bin_type, ncol = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = novel_pal) +

ggsave("plots/biomarathon_barcoding_novel_per_season.png", plot = num_novel_season, 
       height = 7, width = 8, units = "in", dpi = 400)

ggplotly(num_novel_season)

pct_novel_season <- sd %>% 
  filter(!is.na(season)) %>% 
  group_by(bin_type, season) %>% 
  summarise(season_sum = n_distinct(BIN)) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(bin_type)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = season, y = season_sum, fill = bin_type)) + 
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent, breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = novel_pal) + 
  labs(x = "Year-month", y = "Percent of BINs", fill = NULL)

ggsave("plots/biomarathon_barcoding_pct_novel_per_season.png", plot = pct_novel_season, 
       height = 5, width = 8, units = "in", dpi = 400)

ggplotly(pct_novel_season)
```

I'm still not seeing any temporal patterns here as to when we detect novel BINs, but I ran some statistical tests on this to double check.

```{r}
#| label: novel-x-season-test

 sd_seas_wide <- sd %>% 
  filter(!is.na(season)) %>% 
  group_by(bin_type, season) %>% 
  summarise(season_sum = n_distinct(BIN)) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(bin_type)) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = bin_type, values_from = season_sum, values_fill = 0) %>% 
  mutate(total = `Novel BINs` + `Previously in BOLD`) 

m_season <- glm(cbind(`Novel BINs`, total - `Novel BINs`) ~ season, data = sd_seas_wide, family = binomial)
m_season
anova(m_season)

```

After running a GLM on season instead of month, I found the data don't support a seasonal pattern of novel bin detection (χ² = 0.93, df = 3, p = 0.82).

### Depth

Next we wanted to compare novel vs non-novel bins by sampling depth.

```{r}
#| label: novel-x-depth

num_novel_depth <- sd %>% 
  filter(!is.na(Depth_bin)) %>% 
  group_by(bin_type, Depth_bin, Depth_bin_display) %>% 
  summarise(n = n_distinct(BIN), .groups = "drop") %>% 
  filter(!is.na(bin_type)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = Depth_bin_display, y = n, fill = bin_type)) + 
  geom_col() +
  facet_wrap(~bin_type, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = novel_pal) + 
  labs(x = "Depth (m)", y = "Number of BINs", fill = NULL) +
  theme(panel.spacing.y = unit(0.2, "lines"))

ggplotly(num_novel_depth)

ggsave("plots/biomarathon_barcoding_novel_per_depth.png", plot = num_novel_depth, 
       height = 7, width = 8, units = "in", dpi = 400)

pct_novel_depth <- sd %>% 
  filter(!is.na(Depth_bin)) %>% 
  group_by(bin_type, Depth_bin, Depth_bin_display) %>% 
  summarise(n = n_distinct(BIN), .groups = "drop") %>% 
  filter(!is.na(bin_type)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = Depth_bin_display, y = n, fill = bin_type)) + 
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent, breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = novel_pal) + 
  labs(x = "Depth (m)", y = "Percent of BINs", fill = NULL) 

ggplotly(pct_novel_depth)

ggsave("plots/biomarathon_barcoding_pct_novel_per_depth.png", plot = pct_novel_depth, 
       height = 5, width = 8, units = "in", dpi = 400)


table(sd$Depth)

```

Most BINs were shallow, not a big difference in novel/known BINs across depths. I'm noticing the depths are pretty discontinuous, do we want to present the depths as less continuous in the plot (eg, instead of 50m bins, one for 0-11, another for 97-150, a third for 193-270)?

As a first pass I tested the relationship between sampling depth and BIN novelty with a Man-Whitney U test because the depth data are continuous, but aren't normally distributed. I also ran an logistic regression because it can provide more detailed information on the response of BIN novelty to depth and it uses the actual depth values, not just the ranks, which might be important with these discontinuous samplings.

```{r}
#| label: novel-x-depth-test
 
sd_mwu <- sd %>% 
  filter(!is.na(Depth) & !is.na(bin_type)) %>% 
  mutate(Depth = as.numeric(Depth),
         BinType = factor(bin_type)) %>% 
  wilcox.test(Depth ~ BinType, data = .)

sd_mwu

sd_glm <- sd %>% 
  filter(!is.na(Depth) & !is.na(bin_type)) %>% 
  mutate(Depth = as.numeric(Depth),
         BinType = factor(bin_type))  # binomial() will use the 2nd level as "success"

m_depth <- glm(BinType ~ Depth, family = binomial, data = sd_glm)
summary(m_depth)
```

Neither Mann-Whitney U test (p = 0.99) nor the logistic regression (p = 0.38) detected significant associations between bin novelty and depth of sample collection.
